name: Working Memory Load and Environmental Complexity
higher_order_principle: Working memory (WM) has a strict capacity limit (~3-4 items). Environmental features (navigation decisions, instructions, monitoring) consume this capacity. When load exceeds capacity, top-down control breaks down, leading to errors, confusion, and stress.
transferable_to: accessible design (accounting for reduced WM in aging/disability)
scope_conditions: Applies to active tasks, not passive dwelling
Capacity is reduced by stress, fatigue, age
Capacity usage is competitive between task and environment

interactions.description: Offloading information into the environment (signs, maps) reduces internal WM load.
T47 provides the neural implementation (oscillatory dynamics) for the capacity limits described here.

key_references: Buschman & Miller (2010) Frontiers in Human Neuroscience
Luck & Vogel (2013) Trends in Cognitive Sciences
